rows.what the ink shows: After the opening parenthesis, a detached a is followed by two low connected p-like turns, a taller l stroke and the i dot; the following q descends into a long rightward ending. These compressed strokes support applique.

The left curved parenthesis and the large right closing parenthesis survive. Several dense diagonal and horizontal cancellation strokes cross the central letter; the residual short upright and lower stroke do not independently distinguish u.

A thick horizontal cancellation covers nearly the entire former word or glyph. Only two short downward projections remain below the band; no independently readable letter contour survives at fivefold enlargement and increased contrast.

The standalone letter before the equals sign has a shallow rounded bottom and a rising right arm ending in a hooked flourish. Its outline supports v; the u in the following psi(u) has a more extended low two-part course.
Following phi, the left parenthesis joins the small v and makes the combined outline look like two bowls. The v is the right bowl with a tall rising right arm, before a separate closing parenthesis.
Inside the clearly separated parentheses after phi there is one small rounded cup with two upward ends. It is a compact v; the following standalone u is larger and has an additional rightward exit.

Between the closing parenthesis and u is a solid rectangular blue overstroke with rounded corners. The interior is filled, so neither an original single minus bar nor a competing mark can be isolated from the surviving ink.

The opening parenthesis rises from near the phi descender and joins a low rounded v. The dark compact right part ends upward before a distinct closing parenthesis; the joined forms account for the apparent double bowl.

The first word has an open initial c, rounded connected middle strokes and the long terminal run of croissantes. The next cluster has a d ascender, low continuation and detached final s. The last cluster is much paler: only a tall initial stroke and long low ending remain distinct, insufficient to recover all of éléments or exclude an abbreviated form.
Two separate left-facing angle strokes appear between x and the upright 1. Both have an upper diagonal and lower return; the doubled chevrons establish the much-less-than sign.

The phrase starts with a tall open O sweeping into n. The short following group has the compressed e-s-t strokes, and ramené shows the r entry, a small a, linked low humps and a detached acute accent at the end.

Despite the long cancellation through the baseline, the first word retains a small initial bump and raised s/t cluster. After a gap, the n and u humps remain above the line and the final tall l forms an open pointed loop. The surviving sequence supports est nul.
